Title: Quinti Septimii Florentis Tertulliani quae supersunt omnia, Tomus I: libros apologeticos et qui ad ritus et mores Christianorum pertinent
Creator: Tertullian (Quintus Septimius Florens Tertullianus, c. 160-c. 225); Franciscus (Franz) Oehler (editor)
Publisher: Leipzig: T. O. Weigel, 1853 (title page MDCCCLIII)
Publication Date: 1853
Rights: Public Domain (pre-1930 publication); the item record's possible-copyright-status is NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT
Language: lat
Source: Internet Archive item quintiseptimiif04tertgoog, full-text OCR file quintiseptimiif04tertgoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the library/source-research thread (Claude), 2026-09-29. The item record marks possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT (Google scan, contributor University of Lausanne). The item is catalogued as Oehler's 3-volume Quae supersunt omnia; this file is T. 1. Title page read in the OCR: 'QUINTI SEPTIMII FLORENTIS TERTULLIANI QUAE SUPERSUNT OMNIA EDIDIT FRANCISCUS OEHLER ... CONTINENS LIBROS APOLOGETICOS ET QUI AD RITUS ET MORES CHRISTIANORUM PERTINENT LIPSIAE T. O. WEIGEL MDCCCLIII'.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the library thread; the OCR text follows unchanged, apart from this header. Rights basis: the 1853 title-page date clears this registry's public-domain-by-date rule; the host's NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT tag agrees. The Google boilerplate pages at the head of the OCR are left in place. OCR artifacts, running heads, line numbers and apparatus left as found; nothing was corrected, re-spaced or retyped. Measured on the OCR before vendoring: 0 Greek-script characters.
Content note: Contents per the volume's own Index: Ad martyras, De spectaculis, De idololatria, Apologeticum, Ad nationes (2 books), De testimonio animae, De corona, De fuga in persecutione, Scorpiace, Ad Scapulam, De oratione, De patientia, De baptismo, De paenitentia, Ad uxorem (2 books), De cultu feminarum (2 books), De exhortatione castitatis, De monogamia, De pudicitia, De ieiunio, De virginibus velandis, De pallio. An older recension than CSEL: it fills the gap left by the in-copyright CSEL volumes (notably the Apologeticum), and where a work also sits in CSEL 20 or 47 the CSEL text is the better base. Footnote apparatus and superscript siglae are interleaved in the OCR.
